_doc: Revert-verify mutants for the WIRING half of issue #4464: the guards in `helpers/pipe-harness-guards.ts` only protect a harness that actually routes through them. pipe-harness-guards-4464.spec.json locks the guards' BEHAVIOUR (subject = the helper); this spec locks that a driver cannot quietly stop using them (subject = one of the four drivers — a spec has exactly one subject, and the axes enumerate all four `*-pipe.harness.ts` files from disk, so mutating any single one is enough to prove the axis observes them). `create-batch-1848dff9-pipe.harness.ts` is the chosen subject because it is the newest of the four (#4462) and the one whose review surfaced both findings. Expectation written BEFORE the run.
subject: <ABSOLUTE PATH TO YOUR exocortex CHECKOUT>/packages/cli/tests/integration/create-batch-1848dff9-pipe.harness.ts

M1_bundle_path_taken_directly._note: The driver reaches for the bundle path itself instead of asking the guard for it — the pre-#4464 shape, minus even the existence check. Type-preserving (still a `string`). Only G4 reddens: G5 and G6 read different predicates in the same four files, and G1–G3 exercise the helper, which this mutant does not touch. That separation is what makes G4 a statement about THIS driver's wiring rather than about the helper being importable at all.

M2_axes_not_wrapped._note: The axis body runs, but outside the `finally`, so the scratch tree survives a throwing axis again. G6 deliberately stays GREEN — the driver does not grow its own `fs.rmSync` back, it simply stops cleaning up at all, and conflating those two would hide which of them regressed. G4 stays GREEN because the bundle is still obtained through the guard.
